children: Chicago soybeans and corn rose on Monday as traders await a meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, which could generate more Chinese buying of US supplies.
Wheat rose after drone attacks by Ukraine and Russia reduced hopes for a de-escalation in their war which has virtually stopped their Black Sea exports.
Chicago Board of Trade most-active soybeans
rose 0.6% to $13.11-3/4 a bushel at 1132 GMT. CBOT wheat
Dealers await the Trump-Xi meeting from Thursday.

“Soybeans and corn are supported by hopes of more Chinese buying of US supplies if the Trump/Xi talks this week result in some form of trade deal or tariff reductions,” said Matt Ammermann, commodity risk manager at StoneX. “The summit meeting is the dominant market theme this week.”

“Hopes are that if China removes its 10% import duties on US soybeans, import purchases by private Chinese buyers could again resume. Corn could also be part of any US/China trade deal and there are expectations of more US corn sales to Europe if Ukraine’s exports continue to be cut.”
Wheat rose on war disruption to Russia's and Ukraine's exports.

“Wheat is again supported by lack of signs of de-escalation which could permit Russian and Ukrainian ship-borne Black Sea exports to get going again," Ammermann said. "On the contrary, there were massive drone attacks over the weekend, especially by Ukraine on Moscow.”
“It feels like neither Russia nor Ukraine is currently seeking de-escalation or diplomacy which would re-open their Black Sea ports to grain export shipments in the near future.”
Wheat was underpinned by importer demand, with Pakistan buying 365,000 tons on Saturday  and then issuing a tender to buy 185,000 tons on Sunday.
